Faculty are expected to model exemplary professional behavior through work with students, peers, administration, and community colleagues and to provide student support including mentoring, advising, recruiting, and HCAD student project supervision. The successful candidate will teach undergraduate Healthcare Administration courses and, as appropriate, contribute to graduate-level teaching within the College. The faculty member will develop and maintain an active program of scholarship, with scholarly work disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, presentations, and other appropriate venues. The successful candidate will foster relationships with healthcare organizations and community partners, support the development of internships and other experiential learning opportunities, contribute to program assessment and continuous improvement, and participate in activities that advance the goals of CONHS and TAMU-CC. Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with colleagues across disciplines and with healthcare organizations and community partners. Evidence of an active or developing program of research, including peer- reviewed scholarly publications and potential for external funding.

Davis and Loss, the postdoc will collaborate with an interdisciplinary research team that includes: Dr. Omkar Joshi (a social scientist in NREM); past and current OSU graduate students and postdocs funded on the same project; and project stakeholders and partners with state, federal, and tribal agencies. About the Department of Internal Medicine
The Department of Internal Medicine at the University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB) stands at an exciting crossroads of growth and transformation. As we continue Moving Medicine Forward, our focus is on advancing our tripartite mission – delivering high-value care, driving research, innovation, and cultivating excellence in medical education.

The Division of Pulmonary, Critical Care, and Sleep Medicine (PCCSM) at UTMB is a leader in the delivery of advanced respiratory, critical care, and sleep medicine services. With 13 faculty and 12 fellows, the Division combines excellence in clinical care, research, and education to serve patients across UTMB’s three hospital campuses — Galveston, League City, and Clear Lake.

Fellows benefit from exposure to diverse patient populations, advanced technologies, and a collaborative learning environment that promotes professional growth and clinical expertise.
Research within the Division spans clinical, translational, and basic science domains, with active projects in lung cancer and screening, COPD, ILD, pulmonary hypertension, and sleep-disordered breathing. Faculty collaborate across UTMB’s research institutes and centers, supporting innovation that bridges bench to bedside.

 Position Summary Postdoctoral Fellow — Viral Transmission & Vaccine Science Jacco Boon Lab · WashU in St. Louis Want your research to help decide how the next pandemic is stopped? The Boon Lab at WashU Medicine is hiring an enthusiastic Postdoctoral Fellow to join our team studying influenza virus and SARS-CoV-2 infection and transmission in mouse and hamster models. This is a chance to work at the frontier of infectious disease research — using barcoded viruses to track exactly how pathogens spread within and between hosts, and to measure how novel vaccines and environmental factors change the outcome. You won't just run experiments. You'll help answer questions that matter for global public health: How do vaccines and immune responses blunt transmission and disease severity? How do viruses move and disseminate between hosts? Your data will directly shape the design of next-generation countermeasures. About the Boon Lab The Boon Lab studies viral transmission, immune responses, and disease mechanisms while developing diagnostic tools, treatments, and preventive strategies against important human pathogens — including influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and tick-borne viruses such as Bourbon and Heartland virus. The team combines molecular tools, next-generation sequencing, mRNA vaccines, and animal models, and pioneers the use of barcoded viruses to measure and track how viruses replicate, disseminate, and transmit. By pairing cutting-edge technology with collaborations across global health partners, the lab works to unlock the mechanisms driving infection outcomes and to translate that understanding into real-world protection. Where You'll Work The lab is housed in the John T. Milliken Department of Medicine at WashU in St. Louis, MO, on a floor shared with several other laboratories studying virus–host interactions — so collaboration and great science are right outside your door. We also have active, ongoing collaborations with labs across the University, including Molecular Microbiology and Pathology & Immunology. It's a rich, connected environment built for scientists who want to grow. Why This Role • Work with a novel barcoded virus platform few labs in the world can offer. • Build expertise across virology, immunology, and bioinformatics. • Join a collaborative, cross-departmental research community at a top-tier medical school. • Do science with a clear line of sight to real public health impact. Assists in the design of research experiments. Evaluates research findings and assists in the reporting of the results. Conscientious discharge of their research responsibilities. Maintains conformity with ethical standards in research. Maintains compliance with good laboratory practice including the maintenance of adequate research records. Engages in open and timely discussion with their mentor regarding possession or distribution of material, reagents, or records belonging to their laboratory and any proposed disclosure of findings or techniques privately or in publications. Collegial conduct towards co-trainees, staff members and members of the research group. Adherence to all applicable University policies, procedures and regulations. All data, research records and materials and other intellectual property generated in University laboratories remain the property of the University. Working Conditions: This position works in a laboratory environment with potential exposure to biological and chemical hazards. The position will be supported by an NIH-funded R01 project investigating how the nervous system integrates food-related sensory cues to regulate systemic metabolism and aging.A major focus of the project is to determine how sensory information from the dietary environment, including smell and taste, is encoded by neural circuits and translated into systemic physiological responses. We combine Drosophila neurogenetics, optogenetics, connectomics analysis, metabolomics, and lipidomics to investigate how these neural signals reshape systemic metabolism and aging.More broadly, the Lyu Laboratory investigates how the brain interprets environmental information and coordinates responses across neural, endocrine, and peripheral tissues over the life course. Current research examines how sensory experience, nutritional state, and reproductive demands influence longevity, metabolic homeostasis, and age-related functional decline. The laboratory also has a strong computational background and extensive experience developing high-throughput systems for quantitative analysis of behavior and aging, allowing us to connect neural and molecular mechanisms with organism-level phenotypes at scale.Please visit the Lyu Lab website (yanglyu-lab.com) for additional information about the laboratory and our current research.
